title: Best Roofing Software to Manage Crews & Billing (2026)
summary: The best roofing software puts crews, work orders, invoicing, and payments in one place. See what to look for — and how Roofr gets you paid faster.
body_markdown:
TL;DR


Running crews out of group texts and collecting payments through your bank login is how job details slip and invoices sit unpaid. The best roofing software pulls crew scheduling, work orders, invoicing, and payments into one place, so installs start with clarity and end with a job well done.


It’s Monday morning. Your crew is idling outside the wrong address because the install notes were buried in a text thread nobody scrolled back far enough to find. That same morning, last week’s $14,000 invoice still hasn’t gone out because the only person who can log in to the bank has been on a roof since 6 a.m.


Neither of those is a roofing problem. They’re the gaps between the tools you use to run the business, and they’re where the money quietly leaks out.


That’s the real job of a good roofing software: closing the gaps. This is why the best roofing company to manage crews and billing is a software that does BOTH of these things (and ideally, more) in one.


Picture work orders built straight from job data, crew and certification tracking, role-based access so the right people see the right things, and invoicing with card and ACH payments built in. Get those four right and the details stop falling through the cracks between apps.


Here’s how to tell a real all-in-one from a pile of features stitched together.


## **What to look for in roofing crew management software**


Crew management is more than a schedule. When you’re comparing tools, check for these:


- **Work orders that build themselves from the job.** If your team retypes install instructions for every job, that’s wasted time and a missed detail waiting to happen. Look for work orders that pull labor and material line items straight from the proposal or material order.
- **A real crew directory.** Contact info, crew leads, trades, and certifications belong in one system, not in a phone, a whiteboard, and someone’s memory. Certification expiry tracking is a bonus that keeps you compliant without a spreadsheet.
- **Job context attached to the work order.** Photos, measurement reports, and material lists should ride along with the instructions, so the crew shows up knowing the job.
- **Communication that stays tied to the job.** Texting a crew from the platform beats a separate thread that no one can find later.
- **Role-based permissions.** Field crews shouldn’t see your margins, and sales reps don’t need job costs. Control who sees what, once.


## **What to look for in roofing billing software**


Getting the work done is half the job. Getting paid is the other half, and it’s where a lot of roofing companies quietly bleed time. Look for:


- **Invoicing that starts from the signed proposal.** Import the line items and pricing instead of rebuilding the invoice from scratch.
- **Card and ACH payments built in.** Homeowners expect to pay from their phone. In fact, 58% of homeowners say digital payment capability was a deciding factor in choosing a roofer (Roofr 2026 Homeowner Survey). The easier you make it to pay, the faster you get paid.
- **Fees that protect your margin.** Transparent processing rates, no minimums, and the option to pass card fees to the customer keep more of every dollar in your pocket.
- **Team access without exposing your books.** Anyone should be able to send an invoice and request a payment without seeing sensitive accounting details.
- **A dashboard that flags what’s outstanding.** You want to see who’s behind and who’s paid at a glance, not reconcile it by hand.


## **Why one platform beats a stack of tools**


The classic roofing tech setup is a CRM for the pipeline, a separate app for scheduling, texts for the crew, and a bank login for payments. Every handoff between them is a chance for something to fall through.


An all-in-one platform closes those handoffs. The proposal becomes the work order becomes the invoice, and the data carries through instead of getting retyped three times. Matthew Watson of Watchman Roofing went from four platforms down to one after switching to Roofr, and saves 30 minutes a day on admin alone. That’s time back on the roof, or in front of the next homeowner.


Consolidating also means one bill instead of five, and one team to learn instead of a new login every quarter.


## **How Roofr handles crews and billing**


Roofr is built to run a roofing job from the first lead to the final payment in one place. Here’s how the crew and billing pieces fit together.


### **Work orders, built from the job**


With Work Orders in Roofr, you create, send, and track job instructions directly from your jobs. Items marked as labor or other automatically populate the work order, so the crew gets what they need without anyone retyping it. Use templates to keep instructions consistent across jobs, attach photos and measurement reports (or pull them from CompanyCam), and send the whole thing by SMS or email. Every send is logged in the job activity, and calendar events can carry crew details automatically.


### **Crews and certifications in one place**


Roofr Crews lets you manage internal crews and subcontractors without the scattered notes. Store contact info, crew leads, trades, and certifications, and attach licenses and insurance right to the crew.


Set expiry dates on those documents and Roofr notifies you 30 days out, so you’re never sending a crew with a lapsed cert. You can text crews directly from Roofr, and turn on crew approval so a lead formally accepts or rejects a work order — with their name on it — before install day.


### **Permissions that match how you run**


Roofr ships with six standard user roles — Company Admin, General Staff, Sales Representative, Production Manager, Office Admin, and Field Technician — each pre-configured for how roofing companies actually operate. Assign a role, send the invite, done. Need something more specific, like an Insurance Coordinator? Build unlimited custom roles on the Scale plan. Field crews see their jobs and nothing else. The shared-login problem goes away.


### **Invoicing and Payments that get you paid**


Roofr Payments makes card and ACH/EFT payments part of the workflow instead of a separate errand. Convert a signed proposal into an invoice, import the line items, and send a payment request the homeowner can settle from any device. Anyone on your team can create invoices and collect payments without touching sensitive accounting details — so you’re not the bottleneck holding up your own money.


With Platform Fees, you can pass processing costs to the customer and keep your full payout. Take partial payments or deposits, record manual payments (cash and checks) right on the invoice, and watch outstanding balances on the tracking dashboard so you know exactly who to follow up with.


That’s the Amanda Veinott story at Maven Roofing: she used to be the only one who could log in to the bank to create payment links, which put her behind on collecting. Now her admin handles invoicing and payment requests without ever leaving Roofr. In her words, “I am no longer holding us up from receiving money and it’s glorious.”

The best roofing software for crews and billing isn’t the one with the longest feature list. It’s the one that carries a job from proposal to crew to paid invoice without making your team retype the same details three times. If you’ve outgrown a CRM here and a bank login there, a single platform like Roofr is where most roofing companies get their time back — and their cash flow moving.

## **FAQ**


**What is the best software for a roofing company to manage crews and billing?**


The best option is an all-in-one platform that connects your job pipeline to crew scheduling and invoicing, so information carries through instead of getting retyped. Look for work orders built from job data, crew and certification tracking, role-based permissions, and integrated invoicing with card and ACH payments. Roofr combines all of these in one system.

Yes. Roofr Crews lets you manage internal crews and subcontractors in the same place — contact info, crew leads, trades, certifications, licenses, and insurance. You can also request documents from a crew lead and get notified 30 days before a certification expires.


**How do roofing companies get paid faster with software?**


By making it easy to pay. Integrated invoicing and payments let you convert a signed proposal into an invoice, send a payment request the homeowner can pay from any device, and accept card or ACH instantly. Roofr also lets anyone on your team send invoices, so collections don’t wait on one person.

**Can I control what my crew sees in roofing software?**


Yes, with role-based permissions. Roofr offers six standard roles plus unlimited custom roles on the Scale plan, so field technicians see only their assigned jobs while owners and admins keep full visibility into pricing and pipeline.


**Do I need separate software for crews and billing?**


No — and separate tools usually cost you more in lost time than they save. An all-in-one platform keeps work orders, crews, invoicing, and payments connected, which means fewer handoffs, fewer missed details, and one subscription instead of several.
